item.title: Implement safe_extract.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): "Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Context: the repo has SPEC.md, a stub safe_extract.py (5 lines) and test_safe_extract.py with basic tests only. Implement extract(entries, root) -> list[str] exactly as SPEC.md specifies: validate the ENTIRE batch (types, names, duplicates, file/directory collisions in either order, symlinks in root and every existing component, existing-target checks) before creating anything; then create parents and write exact bytes. Reject non-list batches (including tuples, iterators, generators) with ValueError without consuming them. Empty batches return [] after root validation. Unexpected I/O errors must stay visible (no swallowing).

Acceptance: add focused tests covering every error and boundary case in SPEC.md (malformed entries, non-string names, non-bytes data, each name rule, duplicates, collisions both orders, symlinked root, dangling symlink target, symlink ancestor, existing file/dir target, non-directory ancestor, empty batch, empty file, percent signs, validation leaving root unchanged). Use only the Python standard library. Run the test suite and report results. Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the repo's style. Commit the work on the item's branch with a clean commit message (no tool attribution lines). Use only the configured git identity; do not override it.

pr.body:
Approach: safe_extract.py validates the whole batch before creating anything: entry shape, str names (no '/' absolute, '\\', ':', NUL, empty, '.' or '..' components, no normalisation), bytes data, duplicates and file/directory collisions in either order (set-based, order-independent), then walks each target below root rejecting symlinks, non-directory ancestors and existing targets. Only then are parents created and files written with open(..., 'xb'), so existing files are never overwritten. Non-list batches are rejected before the root is checked and without being consumed.

Key files: safe_extract.py, test_safe_extract.py (44 tests in 7 classes, including dangling symlinks, symlinked root and ancestors, validation leaving root unchanged, and an I/O error propagating).

Checks: python3 -m unittest -> 44 OK; ruff check --select E,W,F -> clean.

Review: 4 reviewers (claude-haiku-5-5). review-1 and review-2 passed the whole change at 7f82f13. review-3 failed on the missing wrong-type-root test; fixed in 93ed1a5. review-4 passed the delta from 7f82f13 to 93ed1a5, and a mutation probe confirmed the new test fails when the root check is removed.

Non-blocking follow-ups: case-insensitive/normalising filesystems and names longer than NAME_MAX can fail mid-write after earlier entries are created (SPEC excludes rollback); '' vs Path('') root handling; root reached through symlinked ancestors not checked; message-pinning in some tests; test temp dirs use cwd (dir='.') and repeated setUp.

Assumptions: SPEC's 'Root must be a real directory, not a symlink' is applied to the root path itself; ancestors of root are not checked.

evidence.caption: Before: the stub with the test suite (2 errors)

risk.why: Filesystem-safety code that writes under a caller-supplied root. Guarantees are no symlink following, no traversal, no overwrite, and no collisions. Changes are a new module and its tests only; no existing callers. Reviewers confirmed the rubric level as high.

pr.summary: made safe extraction happen: extract(entries, root) validates the whole batch, then writes exact bytes. now rejects unsafe names, collisions, symlinks, existing targets and bad roots before any write. before: stub raised NotImplementedError, now: 44 passing tests.
